final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers (including regrouping and simplification)

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Determine a least common denominator (LCD/LCM) and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that common denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: The work identifies an LCD/LCM (explicitly or implicitly) for two different denominators
The work scales numerator/denominator to create like denominators prior to subtraction (e.g., a/b → (a·k)/(b·k))
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already the same and no conversion is performed
Only reducing/simplifying a single fraction is done without matching denominators between two fractions

skills.name: Subtract like fractions
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the shared denominator (allowing zero or negative numerator differences).
inclusion_criteria: The work performs a/b − c/b = (a−c)/b (including cases where a−c is 0 or negative)
The work subtracts the fractional components of mixed numbers after denominators are aligned
exclusion_criteria: Only whole-number subtraction is performed with no fraction subtraction
Only converting to a common denominator is shown without executing the subtraction

skills.name: Mixed/whole restructuring
skills.definition: Rewrite mixed numbers or whole numbers into an equivalent form that enables subtraction (e.g., separate whole and fractional parts, convert mixed to improper, or write a whole number as n 0/d).
inclusion_criteria: A whole number is rewritten to include a fractional part with a chosen denominator (e.g., 3 = 3 0/5)
A mixed number is converted to an improper fraction or decomposed as whole + fraction (e.g., 4 1/3 → 13/3; 1 5/3 → 3/3 + 5/3)
A mixed number is re-parenthesized/interpreted to make subtraction well-defined (e.g., 4 − 1 4/3 = 4 − (1 + 4/3))
exclusion_criteria: Borrowing/regrouping from the whole part to fix a negative fractional difference (tag S04 for that action)
Pure fraction-to-common-denominator conversion between two denominators (tag S01)

skills.name: Regroup and simplify result
skills.definition: When needed, borrow/regroup between whole and fractional parts to avoid a negative fractional part, then express the final answer in simplest form (reduce and/or convert to integer or mixed number).
inclusion_criteria: The work borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it to d/d to continue subtraction (e.g., add 12/12, 5/5, etc.)
The work reduces a fraction to lowest terms and/or simplifies 0/b to 0 as part of the final result
The work converts an improper fraction result to a mixed number (or integer) as the final expression
exclusion_criteria: Fraction subtraction is completed with no regrouping and no simplification/final-form conversion is performed
Only finding an LCD (S01) or only subtracting numerators with like denominators (S02) without any regrouping/simplification action

decisions.details: Kept C01 as S01 (Common denominator conversion) with minor wording synthesis from A/B/C.
decisions.reasoning: 3/3 consensus and clearly distinct operation (creating like denominators) that is diagnostically separable from subtraction and simplification.

decisions.details: Renamed C02 from 'Subtract like fractions'/'Subtract fraction parts' variants to S02 'Subtract like fractions' while keeping the same concept.
decisions.reasoning: 3/3 consensus; the chosen name is shortest and applies to both pure fractions and fractional parts of mixed numbers once denominators match.

decisions.details: Refined C03 into S03 (Mixed/whole restructuring) by explicitly listing the three common setup moves: add 0/d, convert to improper, or re-parenthesize as whole + fraction.
decisions.reasoning: 3/3 consensus; refinement improves tagger reliability by distinguishing setup transformations from regrouping (S04) and from common-denominator work (S01).

decisions.details: Refined C04 into S04 (Regroup and simplify result) while keeping regrouping and final simplification/conversion together as in the aligned candidate.
decisions.reasoning: 3/3 consensus and the dossiers show these actions frequently co-occur as the endgame of mixed-number subtraction; keeping them together preserves a compact 4-skill codebook without losing diagnostic coverage.

summary: All four aligned candidate skills had 3/3 expert consensus and mapped one-to-one to the original codebooks, so the final unified codebook keeps all four. Minor refinements were made to improve naming consistency and to sharpen inclusion/exclusion boundaries, especially between mixed/whole setup (S03) and regrouping/simplification (S04).
